read_from: The route text as served: field 1 (the route text) of each row of reader/data/route-store of the main branch at commit 306f3b285898, store_version 87b13b1169b4 (its index.json), for M42: 9,831 routes (axis: routes), 6,705 letters keys (axis: keys). The definition field of the same row equals the route text on 9,831 of the routes. The source audit: each route's store record names one row of the Hebrew table of the lane's copy of PanLex meanings and one row of the English table of PanLex definitions (cointegrated/panlex-definitions, a curator's rearrangement of PanLex's database dump 20250201, in ledgers/work/ldmprs/source-cache/panlex-hebrew-english-2026-07-14/). The English row's column txt equals the record's text on 9,831 of 9,831 records (axis: records), and the column meaning of the English row and of the Hebrew row equals the meaning id the record cites on 9,831 and on 9,831 of them; the record's two other text fields are empty on all of them. So a route comes from one field, one definition on one meaning, the store gives each meaning its own route, and no test here stands on a guess about a field; the audit is evidence about the source and no part of any test. The same English row holds that column example, filled on 9,831 of the records and equal to the record's text on 0: the store did not keep it. The source's own key to its signs: none found. The lane holds 26 files of the curator's and of PanLex's own pages (the curator's READMEs, which say that a definition is a short phrase and txt its text, define the column example as an example of a word for the meaning, and say the database holds "only one word per meaning, chosen arbitrary"; the manifests and the licence page in that folder; the publisher's pages under corpus-lane-builds/moses-works-own-stamp-v1/strand-3-the-publishers/fetch/), and none of them holds a word that names a sign of the text: the search and its word list are the script builder/05-key-search.mjs and its output source-audit/key-search.json. So every shape's meaning here begins "unverified:".

definitions.terms: In every test a character is one Unicode code point (every route holds only characters of 16 bits, so a code point is one index of the JavaScript string). A letter is any character of Unicode category L (JavaScript \p{L}), of any script and in either case; an uppercase letter is one of category Lu. A digit is one of 0 to 9. A space is the character U+0020 only. Nothing is trimmed: the text is the whole route text as it stands, the field route of a line of the by-source JSONL, what the checker gives the classifier, never the field def; the text before and the text after the mark are the template's c.before and c.after; what a bracket holds is the template's c.group, the same for an opener and for its closer; the container and the depth are the template's c.container and c.depth. Directly before and directly after name the one character next to the mark; where the mark stands at that end of the text no character stands there, so a test that asks for a character there fails. A run of letters is a stretch of letters with no other character between them, taken as far as it goes on both sides. The word before the mark is the run of letters that ends directly before the mark, empty if the character directly before the mark is not a letter or none stands there. The word after the mark is the run of letters that begins directly after one space directly after the mark, empty if no space stands directly after the mark or no letter directly after that space. A text holds the word W when one of its runs of letters is exactly W. Begins with means that the first characters are exactly the string, with no need of a word end. The whole text, exactly, means that the text equals the string character for character. A string stands between « and », which are not part of it, and a full stop after » belongs to the sentence and not to the string. Every string and every list minds case and is matched exact to the character.
definitions.first_match: For each mark the shapes are tried in the order they stand in this file; the first whose test holds names the occurrence, and no later shape is tried for it. Not caught above means that no earlier shape of the same mark took the occurrence. A test that names no container holds in any container; a shape's container field is the checker's, compared afterwards.
definitions.unbalanced_text: A text is unbalanced when the ask's helper unbalanced(text) (rule 3 of the ask) returns true on it, the helper copied byte for byte.
definitions.marked_rule: Each entry of marked_rows is one route's text, exact to the character and with nothing trimmed, with the three characters space, pipe, space written directly before each mark the question of the first branch may cut. Each entry of marked_openings is the same for a route too long to quote under the ask's rule 9: the opening of its text, which holds all its marks that may cut, and the entry stops there. Each entry of marked_endings is the same for a route whose first words are too long to quote: it begins with ' | ' directly before the row's first mark that may cut and runs on to the end of the text. A mark stands at a cut when the whole text is equal to an entry of marked_rows once that entry's ' | ' are taken out, or begins with an entry of marked_openings once that entry's ' | ' are taken out, or ends in an entry of marked_endings once that entry's ' | ' are taken out, and in that entry a ' | ' stands directly before this mark: the mark's index in the entry's own text (for an ending, counted from where the ending begins in the text) equals the index of that ' | ' in the entry less three for each ' | ' before it. A row's other marks do not stand at a cut. The lists are tried in that order and the first that names the text decides.

homonyms.reason: The route text carries no entry number, and the source's tables hold no number for a homonym: they give each definition an id and each meaning an id, and a definition with several meanings stands in a row for each. The route store carries neither id; the dictionary store's record keeps the meaning id and the numbers of the two rows in its location field. So two texts under one letters key are two definitions, and the route text cannot say whether two entries or two senses stand behind them. By the audit, of the 1,887 keys with more than one text (axis: keys), 1,886 cite two or more meaning ids and 1 cites one (example key טוב, whose 12 routes cite 12 meaning ids).

branches.question: Some rows give several sayings of one meaning, with a comma or a semicolon between them: rapidly, fast. A few have a colon, a slash or a spaced hyphen there instead. In this dictionary every row is one definition of one meaning, so no sign in the row can tell whether a part means something different from the rest. Today the page may cut such a row at a comma, and never at the other signs. Should these signs cut the row, at the places listed row by row? This ledger as it rests prints each of these rows whole, at the commas too, from the day it is wired. This answer holds whatever you answer to the other questions.

options.means: The page prints each part between the listed places as a reading of its own: rapidly, fast prints rapidly and fast. A label, a bracket or a remark stays with the part it touches, even where it speaks of every part, and nothing is added to the others: figurative: dishonest, illegal prints figurative: dishonest, and illegal with no label. On such a row that is a wrong cut, and this answer takes it. A leading or, and or also stays in its part.
The page prints each row as one reading, as written. At the commas this is a change from today wherever today's rule cuts.

branches.question: Some rows carry marks left over from the source's own files, beside the English: tree of the ''Acer'' genus. The others are web page tags, a wiki's cut-off tail after the words, a table file's doubled quotes, a wiki link's signs, and a colon alone at the head. No key on file says what they are. Should the page print these marks? These marks print until you rule. To leave them out the page needs one step of its own, because the store's text does not change. This answer holds whatever you answer to the other questions.

options.means: The marks stay in what the page prints: O<sub>3</sub>. That holds today and under this ledger. Under this ledger each row prints whole; today the page's own rule still cuts such a row where it has a comma, and the marks print in the pieces.

The page prints the English without these marks, once it has the one step of its own that this answer needs: tree of the Acer genus; O3; automobile for <u>au</u>tomobile; to date for to date {{jump|t|date|s; personal pronoun "he"; Barcelona; sex partner without emotional attachment. Until then the marks print. The store keeps each text as it is.

It leaves to the page the steps that the answers no_pill, without_marks and without_note ask for, since a declaration can cut a row and has no field that leaves a row out or prints part of a text.
